tone.target: thick muff-style grunge fuzz with dark mid crunch
tone.profile: thick muff-style grunge fuzz with dark mid crunch
tone.summary: Gate -> Boost (TS) -> Fuzz (Muff) -> Amp (UK 50/SLP) -> Cab (UK Vintage 4x12) -> EQ -> Delay -> Reverb
corrections: make fuzz primary, not crunch primary

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and noise inherent in high-gain fuzz tones.
Simulate the Tube Screamer boost to tighten up the fuzz and add mid-range punch.
blocks.gap: The GP-180 lacks a dedicated TS model, but Boost is used for gain staging and mid-hump.

blocks.purpose: Provide the core thick, dark grunge fuzz foundation.

alternatives.model: Fuzz (if a more raw, less defined tone is desired)

blocks.purpose: Simulate a British high-gain, mid-focused amp suitable for grunge rock.
blocks.gap: The UK SLP is chosen over the UK 45/50 to balance high gain with classic British tone characteristics.

alternatives.model: UK 45 (for a slightly more aggressive, punchy sound)

blocks.purpose: Provide the required British 4x12 cabinet voicing.
Darken the overall tone and emphasize the dark mid-crunch required for grunge.
Add subtle depth and sustain without sounding too clean or bright.
blocks.gap: Delay is used for ambience, as the target tone is heavy and sustained.

alternatives.model: Tape (for a warmer, less defined echo)

blocks.purpose: Add a subtle sense of space and thickness to the heavy fuzz tone.
blocks.gap: Room reverb is preferred over Plate/Spring as it adds natural, dark ambience suitable for grunge.

alternatives.model: Plate (if more metallic sustain is desired)

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to better capture the raw, dark sound of grunge rock.

proposals.reason: Enhance grit and low-end response for a raw, dark grunge sound.
